name: MARA Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: MARA Holdings, Inc. (formerly Marathon Digital Holdings) is one of the world's largest publicly traded bitcoin miners by hash rate (72.2 EH/s as of Q1 2026) and a major corporate holder of bitcoin. The company is executing a strategic pivot from pure bitcoin mining toward AI/HPC data center infrastructure, with CEO Fred Thiel stating AI compute generates more revenue per electron than mining. Q2 2026 revenue of $174.9M declined 26.7% YoY due to a ~28% lower average Bitcoin price, with a net loss of $611.3M. First-half 2026 revenue was $349.5M versus $452.4M a year earlier. Market cap approximately $3.0B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): MARA scaled hash rate to a record 72.2 EH/s (up 33% YoY in Q1 2026) and expanded to four continents, but revenue declined 26.7% YoY in Q2 and 18% in Q1 as Bitcoin's average price fell approximately 28%, demonstrating that operational execution cannot overcome commodity dependence [1]. The AI/HPC pivot remains entirely pre-revenue despite bold announcements. AI Deployment (1/2): MARA is building AI data center infrastructure with CEO Thiel positioning the company's 900 MW Texas site and other power assets for AI compute — stating 'You get a lot more money per electron if you're doing it for AI than for bitcoin mining' — but no AI products are shipping and no AI revenue has been reported [2]. Market Share (1/2): One of the largest publicly traded Bitcoin miners by hash rate and BTC holdings, but bitcoin mining is increasingly fragmented and the competitive advantage erodes with each halving cycle. Pipeline (0/2): The AI data center pivot, Starwood partnership, and Exaion enterprise AI services represent a plausible pipeline, but specific launch timelines, revenue targets, and customer commitments are absent, and MARA is competing against hyperscalers with dramatically greater resources [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Capital is deployed into mining hardware upgrades, fleet optimization, and power infrastructure acquisition rather than traditional R&D, but the speed of next-gen miner deployment shows technological execution.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): MARA's purpose has shifted from patent monetization to Bitcoin mining to 'digital energy and AI/HPC infrastructure' — a commercially driven narrative that lacks an enduring higher purpose beyond shareholder value and energy arbitrage [2]. CEO Thiel frames decisions around 'more money per electron,' which is financially rational but not inspirational. Community Impact (1/2): MARA has pursued renewable energy initiatives including a landfill methane-powered mining pilot, migration to the King Mountain wind farm, and a 200 MW immersion-cooled facility in Abu Dhabi's Masdar City, demonstrating genuine effort toward carbon neutrality within the crypto mining sector [3]. However, Bitcoin mining energy consumption remains inherently controversial. Employee Retention (1/2): Fred Thiel has led since 2021 with consistent strategic direction through extreme crypto volatility, maintaining a small (~500 person) team across four continents, though no employee engagement or retention data is publicly available. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO Thiel sold 27,505 shares in January 2026, and the company sold a reported $1B in Bitcoin holdings to fund its balance sheet and AI pivot — no meaningful insider buying identified [2].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock. MARA's financial profile is deeply impaired by persistent losses and bitcoin price dependence [1]. D/E of 140.2% scores 0.70 — elevated leverage from convertible notes against cash and BTC holdings of approximately $2.5B combined. ROE of -105.6% scores 0.0 at 2x weight (deeply negative from unrealized mark-to-market losses and operating losses). Revenue growth YoY of -26.7% scores 0.0 (below the -20% floor). Revenue growth 5-year CAGR of approximately 38% scores 1.0 at 2x weight (from ~$159M in 2021 to ~$810M estimated 2026, though this reflects the 2021-2024 BTC bull cycle). Forward P/E of -22.91 scores 0.0 (negative earnings expected). Profit margin of 0% scores 0.0 (breakeven to losses on a GAAP basis). PEG ratio not meaningful with negative earnings, scoring 0 at 2x weight. Weighted sum 2.70/10 yields infrastructure score of 3. Liquidity is ample at ~$344M daily dollar volume [1].

ai_resilience.label: NEUTRAL
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): Bitcoin mining itself is physically intensive — requiring ASIC hardware, massive power infrastructure, and cooling systems — making the computational process immune to AI substitution [1]. However, MARA's entire enterprise value is tethered to Bitcoin, a speculative digital asset whose price AI cannot stabilize or control. The company's own strategic pivot away from mining toward AI compute (CEO Thiel: 'AI delivers more revenue from power than Bitcoin mining') is tacit acknowledgment that AI is reshaping the economics of MARA's business model [2]. The pivot puts MARA in direct competition with hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) and established operators (Equinix, Digital Realty) who possess dramatically greater scale, capital, and customer relationships. AI Opportunity (1/1): MARA's 900 MW Texas site and broader power portfolio position it as a potential AI infrastructure provider, with CEO Thiel framing AI compute as the company's most profitable use of energy. Partnerships with Exaion and Starwood target enterprise and hyperscale AI customers, though this revenue remains entirely pre-commercial [2].

infinite_game.summary: MARA under Fred Thiel operates with opportunistic agility rather than cause-driven purpose. The sequence of pivots — patent monetization, Bitcoin mining, BTC treasury accumulation via convertible debt, AI infrastructure — follows prevailing market narratives rather than advancing a durable mission. While the willingness to pivot demonstrates adaptability, the company plays to win the current cycle rather than to keep playing indefinitely. The $611M Q2 net loss and persistent GAAP unprofitability raise fundamental questions about long-term viability independent of Bitcoin price cycles.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): MARA's purpose remains tethered to financial value creation through energy arbitrage — mining bitcoin, accumulating BTC, and now hosting AI workloads wherever the highest revenue-per-electron opportunity exists [2]. CEO Thiel's framing of decisions in terms of 'more money per electron' is financially rational but not a Just Cause. The company's multiple strategic pivots across patent monetization, crypto mining, and AI infrastructure reflect opportunism rather than an enduring vision of a better future.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): MARA's small team (~500 employees) has shown reasonable stability through extreme crypto volatility, but the company's history includes 2021 investor class-action lawsuits (later dismissed) alleging misleading statements about an OFAC-filtering mining pool, and CEO insider selling during a period of steep stock decline from $11.67 to $7.79 undermines trust signaling [1][3]. No employee engagement or cultural data is publicly available.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): MARA's public communications emphasize scale advantages (largest miner, most power, most BTC held) rather than learning from competitors, and the AI pivot narrative focuses on MARA's unique positioning without constructive acknowledgment of hyperscalers' vastly superior capabilities in AI infrastructure [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): MARA has shown willingness to pivot — from patent monetization to Bitcoin mining to digital infrastructure — and CEO Thiel's statement that AI compute generates more revenue per electron than mining demonstrates intellectual honesty about the business's economics [2]. However, these pivots are driven by financial necessity (declining mining profitability post-halving, BTC price decline) rather than purpose-driven transformation, and execution on the AI pivot remains entirely unproven.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): MARA raised convertible debt to buy Bitcoin during market uncertainty and sold $1B in BTC holdings to fund the AI pivot, demonstrating bold capital allocation [2]. However, these decisions track prevailing market sentiment (buying BTC during the halving cycle, pivoting to AI during the AI boom) rather than contrarian long-term bets, and the $611M Q2 net loss alongside continued strategic bets raises questions about risk management discipline.

investment_thesis: MARA at $7.79 with a $3.0B market cap is a speculative Bitcoin mining and digital infrastructure company whose Inspire Impact Score of 43 (ALIGNED) with zero negative attributions makes it one of the most faith-aligned technology companies in the portfolio [CSV]. CEO Thiel's pivot toward AI data center infrastructure leverages 900+ MW of power capacity, and if Bitcoin prices recover or the AI infrastructure business generates revenue, the stock's 33% decline from $11.67 could represent a contrarian entry point. Hash rate reached a record 72.2 EH/s in Q1 2026 (up 33% YoY) and combined cash and BTC holdings of approximately $2.5B provide some balance sheet cushion [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is severe and multi-dimensional. Q2 2026 revenue declined 26.7% YoY to $174.9M with a $611.3M net loss, and Q1 produced an even larger loss — the company has never generated sustained GAAP profitability [1]. The stock has cratered from $11.67 to $7.79 (down 33%), and D/E of 140% with convertible note obligations creates balance sheet stress if Bitcoin enters a prolonged bear market below $50,000. The AI infrastructure pivot is entirely pre-revenue and competes against hyperscalers and established operators with dramatically greater scale, capital, and customer relationships. MARA's financial performance remains a leveraged derivative of BTC price — purchased energy cost per Bitcoin rose from $32,433 to $39,235, compressing mining economics further [1]. CEO insider selling of 27,505 shares in January 2026, alongside the $1B BTC liquidation, sends a negative conviction signal. ROE of -105.6% and profit margin at breakeven demonstrate fundamental inability to generate returns on invested capital independent of crypto market conditions [1][2].
key_catalysts: AI data center infrastructure monetization — MARA's 900 MW Texas site and power portfolio could begin generating AI/HPC hosting revenue if partnerships with Exaion and Starwood Digital Ventures convert to commercial contracts, potentially reframing the company beyond pure Bitcoin mining [2]

Bitcoin price recovery from the current bear cycle would directly boost mining economics and mark-to-market gains on approximately $2.5B in combined cash and BTC holdings, with the halving cycle historically preceding extended rallies [1]

Inspire Impact Score of 43 (ALIGNED) with zero negative attributions provides a rare faith-based allocation opportunity in the digital infrastructure space, which may attract ESG and values-oriented capital [CSV]
key_risks: Persistent GAAP losses ($611M net loss in Q2 2026) and D/E of 140% with convertible note obligations create existential risk if Bitcoin remains depressed and the AI pivot fails to generate revenue — the company has never demonstrated sustained profitability [1]

AI infrastructure pivot competes against hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) and established operators (Equinix, Digital Realty) with dramatically greater scale, capital, and customer relationships — MARA has zero track record in enterprise AI hosting and the pivot is entirely pre-revenue [2]

Revenue concentration in Bitcoin mining means financial performance remains a leveraged derivative of BTC price, with purchased energy costs rising from $32,433 to $39,235 per Bitcoin, compressing margins even as hash rate grows — the business model breaks at sustained BTC prices below $40,000 [1]
